title: Describing Data: Mean, Median, Mode, and Spread

questions.question: For the data 4, 7, 7, 8, 9, 14, what is the median?
questions.rationale: Sorted data has six values; the median is the average of the middle two: (7+8)/2 = 7.5.

questions.question: Why do news reports usually quote median salaries rather than mean salaries?
options: A few very high incomes distort the mean upward
questions.rationale: Income is right-skewed: extreme values drag the mean up, while the median still describes a typical earner.

questions.question: Two datasets both have mean 50: {49, 50, 51} and {0, 50, 100}. What differs between them?
questions.rationale: Centres match but spread differs enormously — the first is tightly clustered, the second wildly scattered.

questions.question: Which measure of centre is the only one that makes sense for categorical data like 'most common shoe size'?
questions.rationale: You cannot add or order categories numerically; the mode — the most frequent value — is the only applicable measure.

questions.question: In a right-skewed distribution (long tail of large values), the typical relationship is:
questions.rationale: The long right tail pulls the mean above the median — which is why the median is trusted for incomes and house prices.

questions.question: For the test scores 4, 7, 7, 8, 9, 14, what is the mean (approximately)?
questions.rationale: The mean is the sum divided by the count: (4+7+7+8+9+14)/6 = 49/6 ≈ 8.2; it is dragged up by the outlier 14.

questions.question: What is the mode of the dataset 4, 7, 7, 8, 9, 14?
questions.rationale: The mode is the most frequent value; only 7 appears twice in this dataset.

questions.question: How is the range of a dataset calculated?
options: Sum of values divided by count
Average of the squared deviations from the mean
Spread of the middle 50% of values
questions.rationale: Range = maximum − minimum. It is crude but instant; the middle-50% description belongs to the IQR.

questions.question: Which measure of spread is immune to outliers?
questions.rationale: The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data, so extreme values cannot affect it — unlike the range or standard deviation.

questions.question: In a symmetric distribution (e.g., adult heights), what relationship holds between mean and median?
questions.rationale: In a symmetric shape there is no long tail on either side, so the mean and median roughly coincide.

questions.question: An easy exam where most scores are high but a few very low scores stretch one tail produces a left-skewed distribution. What is true then?
questions.rationale: Left-skew means the long tail points down toward small values, dragging the mean below the median.
